content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict on a single verse (Matthew 1:16), so the rule governing what may ground such a verdict applies.", "verdict": "CLEAN", "quote": "the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.", "room": "'does not state a link or its contrary' — read narrowly as silence/non-statement, versus read broadly as any failure of a single verse to decide the question. The judge grounds the verdict on what the verse does state (passive verb, feminine pronoun) being compatible with both readings, and on the parties' actual answers, not on the verse's silence about a link.", "why": "The UNDERDETERMINED verdict rests on the verse's positive wording being genuinely ambiguous between the two answered readings, not on the absence of an express statement, so it does not use non-statement as a ground."}
